title: FRED Adds Median Inflation Data from the Cleveland Fed
gist: FRED Blog note that FRED now hosts the Cleveland Fed's median PCE inflation series (Feb 1970–Sep 2026, YoY and MoM), explaining how the median filters out extreme category price swings to track underlying inflation, alongside trimmed-mean and sticky-price alternatives.

insights.claim: FRED has added the Cleveland Fed's median PCE inflation data, covering February 1970 to September 2026 in both year-over-year and month-over-month form.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: A free, long-history underlying-inflation series is now easy to chart against headline and core PCE for Fed-path analysis.

insights.claim: Median PCE inflation is computed by ranking the price changes of all individual PCE spending categories and taking the middle value, so it is unaffected by extreme moves such as gasoline spikes or airfare dips.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: When headline is distorted by energy or volatile items, median PCE gives a cleaner read on the breadth of inflation the Fed cares about.
insights.quote: The median is not impacted by what happens at the extremes of price swings, only by broad changes in the distribution of price changes.

insights.claim: Trimmed-mean inflation, a close cousin of the median measure, drops the components with the largest and smallest price changes and averages the rest, while the median trims everything but the middle; FRED also carries the Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE, the Cleveland Fed trimmed-mean CPI and the Atlanta Fed sticky-price CPI.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Triangulating median, trimmed-mean and sticky-price measures helps distinguish broad-based from narrow inflation pressure.
insights.locator: More inflation trend data in FRED
